# `async` dialect

Structured-concurrency ops (sec 37): tokens / waits / joins / race / cancellation, host-only.

**6 ops:** `await`, `cancel`, `join`, `launch`, `race`, `scope`

## `async.await`

Wait for a token; produce the async body's yielded values.

async.await(%token) -> (%v...). Consumes %token EXACTLY once (use-once, sec 116) and yields the launched body's values. Reference executor (CEIR-6b): returns the body's yield.

## `async.cancel`

Cancel a pending async operation (consumes its token).

async.cancel(%token). Consumes %token -- ⛔ every token is awaited XOR cancelled, NO silent drops (an unconsumed token is a find_token_misuse Unconsumed). Cancellation PLUMBING through the provider lands at CEIR-6c.

## `async.join`

All-of: consume N tokens; produce one token that completes when all of them do.

async.join(%t...) -> %token. Consumes each operand token ONCE (TokenConsumer) and produces a NEW token (TokenProducer) that completes when all inputs do. join carries BOTH traits.

- **Version:** 1
- **Traits:** `TokenProducer`, `TokenConsumer`
- **Regions:** 0
- **Effects:** `Synchronization`

| `token` | any | a new completion token for the whole group |

**Attributes:** _none_

## `async.launch`

Structured async fork: run the region asynchronously and produce a completion token.

async.launch { body } -> %token. Structured concurrency (sec 30): the body runs asynchronously; %token represents its completion (its yielded values are what await produces). ⛔ EXECUTOR CONTRACT (CEIR-6b): the body runs at an UNSPECIFIED later time; the SEQUENTIAL REFERENCE executor runs it AT launch and %token completes when the body's yield is reached.

- **Version:** 1
- **Traits:** `TokenProducer`
- **Regions:** 1
- **Effects:** `Synchronization`

**Operands:** _none_

**Results:**

| `token` | any | the completion token -- consume EXACTLY once (await / join / race / cancel) |

**Attributes:** _none_

## `async.race`

Any-of / select: consume N tokens; produce the index of the first ready.

async.race(%t...) -> %index. Consumes each operand token once; produces the WINNER'S INDEX (a value-CARRYING race needs async-value types -> CEIR-6b/6c, named). Nondeterministic (the order of readiness is not fixed) -- so it is illegal under CertifiedDeterministic/Deterministic compiler mode (CEIR-4b).

- **Version:** 1
- **Traits:** `TokenConsumer`
- **Regions:** 0
- **Effects:** `Synchronization`
- **Determinism:** `Nondeterministic`

**Results:**

## `async.scope`

A structured-concurrency scope (sec 30): a region whose dynamic extent ends only when every token launched inside it is consumed.

async.scope { ... } -> (%r...). Structured concurrency (sec 30): the scope OWNS the tokens launched inside it -- its dynamic extent ends only when every one is consumed. ⛔ SCOPE-CONFINEMENT is LAYERED verification, not new code: 5b SSA-scoping already blocks consuming a scope-launched token in a SIBLING region (UseBeforeDef), and 6a use-once already blocks leaking it (Unconsumed) or yielding it OUT (ConsumedByNonConsumer) -- a token is confined to its scope's dynamic extent by construction. Declares an ambient Synchronization effect (its exit is a JOIN point -- a blocking wait) -> illegal in an audio-RT region (correct: a join-at-exit blocks). ⛔ EXECUTOR CONTRACT: the SEQUENTIAL reference is a no-op boundary (everything already completed at launch -- it just forwards the region's yield); the JOBS-BACKED provider joins outstanding work at scope exit (the slice that needs concurrent async semantics).

- **Version:** 1
- **Traits:** _none_
- **Regions:** 1
- **Effects:** `Synchronization`

**Operands:** _none_

| name | type | doc |
| --- | --- | --- |
